senses.d: The physics of light and vision: basic optical science.

senses.d: Technology that makes use of such physics: applied optical science; business lines making use of such technology.

senses.d: The light-related aspects of a device.

ety.text: From French option, from Latin optiō (“choice; option; act of choosing”), from optō (“to choose, select”). Equivalent to opt + -ion.

senses.d: One of a set of choices that can be made.
The freedom or right to choose.

A contract giving the holder the right to buy or sell an asset at a set strike price; can apply to financial market transactions, or to ordinary transactions for tangible assets such as a residence or automobile.

The acquiring or retention of a nationality through personal choice as a right, bypassing selective legal mechanisms for naturalization, especially in cases where a territory is transferred or passed on from one state to another.
ex: This group constitutes around 9 percent of the total number of acquisitions of Dutch nationality through option.

senses.d: To purchase an option on something.
ex: The new novel was optioned by the film studio, but they'll probably never decide to make a movie from it.

senses.d: To configure, by setting an option.
ex: The device that is to echo the characters should be optioned for echoplexing.

grp.label: one of the choices that can be made
